claims.statement: dcode create_model applies its allowlist after provider inference but before credential bridging, provider profiles, and provider imports; blocked models therefore cannot cause those side effects.

The SDK exposes orthogonal beta profile registries: ProviderProfile controls string-model construction through init_chat_model, while HarnessProfile controls prompt, tools, middleware, and default-subagent behavior after model construction; both accept provider or provider:model keys and registration layers rather than replaces existing settings.

Provider-profile resolution merges an exact model profile over its provider profile, chains pre-initialization hooks and dynamic factories base first, and lets factory output override static profile kwargs while caller kwargs retain final precedence.

Harness-profile lookup selects an exact spec before provider fallback and merges model-level and provider-level fields; create_deep_agent resolves this profile for the main model and each declarative subagent before applying prompt, tool-description, and middleware changes.

Profile bootstrap is lazy, thread-coordinated, and one-time: built-ins load by direct imports, then third-party provider and harness entry-point hooks layer on top; broken built-ins fail bootstrap while broken third-party plugins are logged and skipped.

SDK resolve_model applies ProviderProfile construction behavior only to string specifications and returns an existing BaseChatModel unchanged; focused tests cover both pass-through and profile-derived kwargs for string resolution.

dcode creates models only after policy validation, layers provider and per-model defaults with stored credentials and SDK provider profiles before runtime kwargs, and stamps the concrete model with the provider-specific retry budget used after runtime model switching.

dcode's ModelCatalog is a strict presentation snapshot that carries model specifications, provider readiness, policy metadata, and a scalar allowlist of displayable capability fields with override provenance; it does not cross constructor kwargs or arbitrary profile extensions over the process boundary.

dcode discovery filters profile-derived models to enabled providers with tool calling and usable text I/O, merges explicitly configured model lists, and then applies models.allowed; recommended and current specifications are retained only when provider enablement and policy permit them.

dcode reports provider readiness independently from discovered model rows, including setup hints for known custom or credential-mapped providers; a remote picker uses the supplied catalog rather than local provider data, and applies catalog policy before provider installation or authentication prompts.

ConfigurableModelMiddleware can switch a model and merge per-call settings from runtime context without recompiling the graph; blocked switches propagate, while other construction errors can fall back to the current model unless strict resolution is enabled.

dcode exposes reasoning effort only from a reasoning-capable model profile, normalizes provider-native effort parameters to reasoning_effort, and restricts Anthropic between-tools mode to low, medium, and high effort levels.

dcode disables recognized provider SDK retry loops, stores the selected retry budget on each constructed model, and its model-node middleware uses that per-request budget so runtime model switches do not multiply retry attempts.

CodeModelRetryMiddleware retries only classified transient model failures at the model node, uses provider Retry-After or jittered exponential backoff within an interactive delay budget, re-raises failures instead of fabricating an AI answer, and emits attempt and retry lifecycle events for streamed-output reconciliation.

Harness profiles can tune every SDK-assembled main, general-purpose, and declarative synchronous subagent stack through static or factory extra middleware, but cannot inject into already compiled or remote async subagents; file-friendly HarnessProfileConfig deliberately excludes this runtime-only extension.

Harness middleware exclusions cannot remove required filesystem or subagent scaffolding, and unmatched exclusions fail graph assembly; tool exclusions instead run after tool-injecting and custom middleware, making them the supported way to hide tools from the model.
dcode pins its SDK dependency to deepagents==0.7.32, supplies core Anthropic, Google GenAI, and OpenAI integrations, and exposes additional model integrations as optional provider extras.
dcode captures the DEEPAGENTS_HOME-selected profile at launch as the PATHS trust root, so dotenv files and later directory/configuration changes cannot redirect its config or state locations.

dcode capability profiles are a separate descriptive layer: get_model_profiles merges upstream integration profile data with configured and CLI overrides, tracks overridden keys, and includes configured-only, class-path, Codex, and discovered Ollama models.
An explicitly malformed dcode models.allowed declaration becomes a deny-all policy rather than silently falling back to unrestricted model access.
dcode registers a prompt-only HarnessProfile for three exact GLM-5.2 provider specifications before CLI graph creation, idempotently preserving an existing suffix profile for a specification.

Only headless dcode stacks install GLM terminal-stall recovery; for the exact Fireworks GLM-5.2 spec, one tool-free AI result classified as max-output-token truncation gets at most one forced-tool retry with reasoning disabled, while interactive and other-provider GLM calls do not recover.

Harbor evaluation construction calls init_chat_model directly and therefore explicitly supplies the OpenAI Responses API default; for the shared exact GLM-5.2 specs it defaults nested reasoning effort to high only when callers supplied no native effort setting.

dcode normalizes provider truncation metadata and turns a main-agent reply that is both truncated and devoid of visible text or tool calls into a typed error, preventing an empty reply from being checkpointed as an apparently successful run; truncated subagents instead return an empty failure to their parent or retain partial content with a warning.

After policy admission, dcode bridges stored credentials before its explicit-provider credential check, skips that check for implicit-auth providers, and reports missing credentials as a typed actionable error.

The effective dcode model-node retry budget is selected in descending precedence from --max-retries, provider-specific retry configuration, global retry configuration, and the built-in default; zero disables retries.
dcode converts arbitrary ProviderProfile hook or factory failures into ModelConfigError so model-construction failures use the application's actionable error path.
